question.problem:
Which of the following are logically equivalent to $P?$

I. $P∧(Q∨P)$

II. $Q∧(P∨Q)$

III. $(Q∨P)∧P$
question.worked_solution:
The law that conjunction absorbs disjunction is stated as

$$
P∧(P∨Q)≡P.
$$

With that in mind, let's inspect each of the given statements.

- Statement I is logically equivalent to $P.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}P∧(Q∨P) & ≡P∧(P∨Q) \\  & ≡P.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

- Statement II is *not* logically equivalent to $P.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}Q∧(P∨Q) & ≡Q∧(Q∨P) \\  & ≡Q≢P.\,\times \end{aligned}
$$

- Statement III is logically equivalent to $P.$ We have

$$
\begin{aligned}(Q∨P)∧P & ≡P∧(P∨Q) \\  & ≡P.\,✓\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, the correct answer is "I and III only."
